recipes.name: Touchdown Chili
ingredients_raw: 1 (28 ounce) can diced tomatoes with juice
1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle beer
1 (4 ounce) can diced green chile peppers, drained

steps.text: Cook and stir ground beef, onion, and garlic in a large pot over medium heat until beef is crumbly and no longer pink and onion is tender. Drain excess fat. Season ground beef mixture with chili powder, cumin, and basil; cook and stir over medium heat until ground beef is evenly coated and spices are toasted.

Stir in tomatoes, tomato sauce, beer, chile peppers, and vinegar; bring to a boil while scraping the brown bits of food off the bottom of the pan. Stir in brown sugar, salt, hot pepper sauce, and black pepper.
Reduce heat to low, cover the pan, and simmer for 3 hours, removing the lid for the last 30 minutes of cooking.

raw_recipe.headline: Touchdown Chili
raw_recipe.description: This touchdown chili recipe simmers ground beef and onion for hours with juicy tomatoes, beer, hot sauce, and vinegar — perfect for football season

review.reviewBody: I know some people are hesitant to try recipes that have only been rated by a couple folks, but this one you must try! The combinations of the pepper/hot and the brown sugar, along with the bitterness from the vinegar and beer...there are so many hearty flavors that truly make this delicious. I didn't change a thing! Thank you!

I added about 1 tsp cayenne, as my kids like spicy, and it had a nice but not too overwhelming burn. I also used my instant pot, and I cooked on manual for 20 minutes, then did a quick release. I simmered for 30 minutes uncovered to allow some liquid to evaporate. I will definitely be making this again!

This recipe is fantastic as is. This is now my go to chili recipe. Everyone in my family absolutely loves it. I’ve done different things with the recipe just based on what I had on hand – without the beer for instance. The one thing I do regularly is use a pound of hamburger and half pound of pork sausage. I’ve also used ground turkey as others mentioned. We do like beans, so I usually add one can of light red kidney beans or some other chili being near the end of the cooking time.Most of the time I mix everything up and then put it in the crockpot for several hours rather than on top of the stove just so I can forget about it until dinner. We do like beans, so I usually add one can of light red kidney beans or some other bean near the end of the cooking time. You cannot go wrong with this recipe!

Very good, but I made some changes. I used about 2.5 lbs of meat (ground turkey), so the 1/3 cup of chili powder worked well. I omitted the beer entirely to make this a gluten-free dish. I did add the vinegar, but also about a tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce. I used Chipotle Tabasco (1 teaspoon) and only added about 1/2 teaspoon of Himalayan sea salt. (I am on a low-sodium diet.) Once it started to boil, I moved it to the Crockpot and let it simmer on high for an hour before digging in. While eating, I let the rest continue simmering for another 2 hours.

I absolutely love this recipe! I make it often and it's always a huge hit with my family. I add a 24 ounce can of spicy baked beans, some chopped bell pepper, reduce the brown sugar by half, omit the vinegar and, since i grew up eating Cincinnati chili, I added 2 teaspoons of ground cinnamon. Then I pour it all into the slow cooker for 6 to 7 hours. amazing! kiddos to the poster of this awesome recipe! :-)

Oh, this is good! We live in southern New Mexico, so please, be prepared for some heat if you try my adjustments. I halved this recipe, added extra green chiles, like 8 ounces of fresh roasted green chile, I also added a tsp. of cayenne and a good sprinkle of pepper flakes and served over zucchini noodles (low carbin" it) with a healthy (and I mean large) topping of jalapeno jack and cheddar. With a salad, this was an amazing dinner!!!

I made this chili and thought it was really good. I first made this without the beer, vinegar, brown sugar and hot sauce. It definitely tasted as though it was missing something. I then added the beer, vinegar, brown sugar and hot sauce. Although I thought the vinegar was going to be a weird addition it was not. I also added green pepper and red kidney beans. Will be making this again.

Excellent! A very comfortable (no sweat, no tears) and tasty heat from this traditional chili. 

Modifications:
- Made it with an IPA 
- Added 1 can of white kidney beans (it could have even used another can).
- Cooked for longer than 30 minutes with the lid off...closer to
90 minutes

This is an excellent recipe with no changes. I’m not a fan of beans in chili so this works really well. I used the leftovers to make an appetizer. Spread cream cheese on the bottom of a 9 inch pie plate. Top with 2 cups of touchdown chilli mixed with half a cup of sour cream. Top with texmex cheese and bake in the oven on 350 for 20 minutes. Served with a baguette. It was amazing!

Fantastic recipe - I was worried about the vinegar and brown sugar, but that with the beer takes this chili all the way into flavor town! I did saute a few seeded jalapenos and a poblano with the meat. To add additional flavor dimension, I added two packets of concentrated liquid beef stock. This will be our go to chili recipe forever. Thanks so much!

First time making this and it came out amazing. I did take Kim's recommendations and substituted 1 lb of the beef with 1 lb of pork sausage along with the pumpkin puree in for the tomato sauce. I removed the vinegar and used Sapporo beer (rice beer), thanks kandygirl. I also lessened the chili powder amount to 1/4 cup and add a bit of cinnamon due to my love of Cincinnati chili. It finished not 5 minutes ago and I couldn't have asked for a better chili. This alteration of the recipe is good for those that can't take a lot of heat but love enough of it.

Once I made this chili it became "our" chili recipe :). I add beans (2. Light red and 2 dark red) my husband loves beans! And I usually chop up a jalapeno and toss it in. I never have beer on hand because we don't drink so I sub beef broth. I really want to try it with beer one time to see the difference!

I needed a 'no beans' chili recipe because my husband is a 'no beans' kind of guy. I found this one years ago and have never used another chili recipe since....it's the VERY BEST! Even better the next day..'try it, you'll like it' :)

Outstanding! Changes I made: Used a can of Hot diced green chiles. (Heat was just right... could use a touch more.. will add a little cayenne next time). Added a can of Dark Red kidney beans... I'll probably add another can of a different bean next time. Very Very Good!

By far the best chile recipe I’ve tried! Super tasty and rich with flavor. Sometimes I add a can of beans and a little extra tomato sauce, just for more protein and fiber, but as a bean-less chili I wouldn’t change a thing!
LOVE this recipe!! Amazing flavor and easy! No beans and the beer gives it a different taste! My go to!!!
Made this numerous times ... Its great the way it is !
